clue.text: A final send-off in two ways?

definitions.text: A final send-off in two ways?

parts.words: A final send-off in two ways?
parts.note: one send-off is the bugle call sounded at a military funeral, the other is the day's last collection of letters from a postbox

explanation.walkthrough: The 'two ways' are a farewell to the dead and the final dispatch of mail; both are a closing send-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom twice over: the bugle call ending a soldier's funeral and the last mail collection of the day each send something off.

clue.text: Who pays the rent? I suggest we look, but there's no time

indicators.note: there's no says the following letter is missing

parts.note: a proposal to take a look is 'let's see'

explanation.surface: A landlord asks who pays the rent and proposes checking, but lacks the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a tenant holding a lease is the party who pays rent to the landlord.

clue.text: Garment is in appropriate, but women will go for it

indicators.note: will go for says one piece takes the place of another

parts.note: read as one word, inappropriate means wrong
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A garment is called inappropriate, but women will like it anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in appropriate' must be closed up into 'inappropriate'. 'It' as sex appeal is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sarong is a length of cloth wrapped round the waist, worn in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Grant perhaps provides homeowner with a little money upfront

indicators.note: upfront says the first piece is placed at the front

parts.note: P stands for penny, a small amount of money
a resident is someone who lives in a home

explanation.surface: A grant gives a homeowner a small sum in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a payment; it is Ulysses S. Grant, US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Ulysses S. Grant was the eighteenth head of state of the United States.

clue.text: Use threat to unsettle daughter? That's brave!

indicators.note: unsettle means disturb, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A parent bullies their daughter with threats, and calls it brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone resolute and courageous in the face of danger is brave.

clue.text: Spots crook coming from hearing

indicators.note: coming from hearing says we want a word that sounds like the one the clue word gives

parts.note: to crook an arm or finger is to bend or flex it

explanation.surface: A criminal is identified by what a witness overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like a criminal, but it is the verb for bending a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: small marks or specks of colour on a surface are spots.

clue.text: Capital city covering area within bounds of Himalayas

indicators.note: covering says this piece wraps around the rest

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: within says this letter goes inside the outer letters
bounds of asks for the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A capital city occupying a region in the Himalayas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital city' reads as one phrase; split, 'Capital' defines and 'city' gives LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Lhasa is the chief city of Tibet, high in the Himalayan region.

clue.text: Female figure supporting a charity devastated — husband dropped dead

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
dropped says this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A woman who supported a charity is devastated after her husband dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devastated' rearranges A CHARITY; 'dropped' takes out H to leave CARYATI, then D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a caryatid is a carved woman used as a column holding up an entablature.

clue.text: Fair game

definitions.meaning: fair as in decent and generous towards an opponent
game as in willing to have a go

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: behaving decently to opponents, and being willing to take part in something.

clue.text: Inspector is right to arrest suspect voyeurs? On the contrary

indicators.note: arrest says one piece holds another inside it
On the contrary flips the roles, so the jumbled voyeurs hold the right letter, rather than the other way round
suspect, as an adjective, says the letters of voyeurs are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A police inspector arrests suspected peeping toms.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, R would hold the anagram; 'On the contrary' turns it round so the rearranged VOYEURS (SUVEYOR) holds R.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a surveyor is someone who inspects buildings or land professionally.

clue.text: A place to drink port in Spanish district

parts.note: a bar is a place where drinks are served
Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Where to have a glass of port in a Spanish neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink, but it is the harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish loan word: a barrio is a quarter or neighbourhood of a Spanish-speaking town.

clue.text: Loosely speaking, cello's not a musical instrument

indicators.note: Loosely means not tightly arranged, so the letters are rearranged
not says the following letter is taken out of the pool

parts.note: cello is used as written; the 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: A pedant says the cello, strictly speaking, isn't a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loosely speaking' reads as a phrase, but 'Loosely' rearranges SPEAKING and CELLO, and 'not a' removes A.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a glockenspiel is a percussion instrument of tuned metal bars struck with hammers.

clue.text: Boredom affected 9 Across you said?

indicators.note: Across here means lying across, so the letter is spread over by the jumbled number
affected means altered, so the letters of the number are rearranged

parts.note: the figure 9 is written out as the word nine

indicators.note: said tells us to take the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: the word you is pronounced like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone reports that the answer to 9 Across bored them.
explanation.walkthrough: '9 Across' looks like a cross-reference but is the number nine; 'affected' makes ENNI, and 'Across' sets that around U.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: listless weariness from lack of interest, a French loan word for tedium.

clue.text: To distinguish between hill and a pike primarily needs skill

parts.note: a tell is an ancient mound in the Middle East built up from layers of settlement

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of the word it follows

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Telling a hill from a pike, a northern word for a peak, takes expertise.
explanation.walkthrough: TELL is a crossword favourite for an archaeological mound.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to tell two things apart is to discriminate or differentiate between them.

clue.text: Fire half obliterated the kitchen — that's a result!

indicators.note: half obliterated says one half of the word is wiped out, leaving the other half

parts.note: the word fire is taken as written
the kitchen is orchestral slang for the percussion section

explanation.surface: A fire has gutted half the kitchen, and someone exclaims at the consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half obliterated' removes the first half of FIRE, leaving RE. 'That's a result!' is British slang for a good outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a repercussion is a consequence or after-effect of an action.

clue.text: Advice for someone with dangerous habit like coke?

definitions.text: Advice for someone with dangerous habit
definitions.meaning: the counsel given to a heavy smoker: cut down on cigarettes
coke is a fuel that burns without producing fumes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Coke' suggests cocaine, matching the 'dangerous habit'; it is the solid fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a two-word suggestion to cut down on cigarettes, and descriptive of fuel burning without fumes.

clue.text: A container like this is needed for prickly plant

parts.note: a can is a metal container
thus means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A container of this kind is needed for a spiny plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: acanthus is a spiny-leaved Mediterranean plant whose leaves inspired Corinthian columns.

clue.text: Completely and thoroughly defeat leaderless Tories

indicators.note: leaderless says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to rout an army is to defeat it thoroughly
the Tories are the party of the political right

explanation.surface: A call to crush the Conservatives entirely, now they have no leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaderless' seems to describe the Tories but trims the piece before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something done wholly and without reservation is done completely.

clue.text: Once torture's deployed to secure information, finally he'll sing

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the jumble holds a letter inside
deployed means arranged differently, so the letters are rearranged
finally asks for the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Once torture is used to extract information, the victim will finally sing, that is, confess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sing' is the criminal sense of confessing; here the definition is literal. 'deployed' makes COUTERTENOR, which holds N.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a male singer with a voice above tenor, so he is someone who sings.

clue.text: Household's staff get on

parts.note: staff are the men employed
to get on is to grow older, to age

explanation.surface: The servants of a household get along together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on' suggests getting along; it means growing old.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a French loan word for the members of a domestic establishment.

clue.text: First signs of cannabis cause arrest I see — it's a plant

indicators.note: arrest says those letters hold the next one
First signs of asks for the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, the see of a bishop

explanation.surface: Spotting traces of cannabis leads to an arrest, an officer reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a bishop's diocese; 'I see' is not a phrase here.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: sweet cicely is an aromatic herb of the carrot family.

clue.text: Endless waiting when detained by head produces apprehension

indicators.note: detained by says this piece is held inside the next one

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

indicators.note: Endless says the outer letters of the word are cut off

parts.note: serving, as at table, is waiting

explanation.surface: Being kept waiting by the headteacher makes a pupil anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests a headteacher; it is a headland. 'Endless' trims SERVING to ERVIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: anxious unease about what may happen is both apprehension and nerviness.

clue.text: Relatively risky, heading off with increased chance of freezing

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter is removed

parts.note: relatively risky means more chancy, the comparative of dicey

explanation.surface: Conditions grow riskier, and the frost is coming on.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative: colder conditions bring the temperature nearer to the point where water turns solid.

clue.text: Varnish can be made with this component of diesel emissions

definitions.text: Varnish can be made with this

indicators.note: component of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Varnish might be made from something present in exhaust fumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a tropical tree resin used in making varnishes and ointments.

clue.text: Type of food that fills the stomach

definitions.text: Type of food that fills the stomach

parts.words: Type of food that fills the stomach
parts.note: read as a hearty meal, but this Scottish dish of offal and oatmeal is literally stuffed into a sheep's stomach to cook

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fills the stomach' sounds like filling food; the dish is cooked inside a sheep's stomach casing.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal description: a Scottish pudding of sheep's offal, oatmeal and suet boiled in the animal's stomach.

clue.text: Mutt and Jeff at last will leave pretty Derbyshire village

indicators.note: will leave says that letter departs from the words that follow

parts.note: fair means pretty, as in a fair maiden

indicators.note: at last asks for the final letter of the name

parts.note: Edale is a village in the Peak District of Derbyshire, start of the Pennine Way

explanation.surface: Two cartoon characters, Mutt and Jeff, leave a picturesque English village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mutt and Jeff' is a comic strip (and rhyming slang for deaf), but 'and' just joins; Mutt is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Airedale is a breed of terrier, and a mutt is slang for any dog.

clue.text: Spelling's almost woeful preceding enlightenment?

indicators.note: preceding says the first piece comes before the second
almost says the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: woeful means sad
Tori Spelling is an American actress, so Spelling's first name is Tori

explanation.surface: A bad speller's dismal effort comes before some sort of enlightenment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spelling' suggests orthography, but it is the surname of actress Tori Spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: satori is the sudden enlightenment sought in Zen Buddhism, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Stormy petrel's tail is grabbed by dude unknown

indicators.note: is grabbed by says this letter is seized inside the next piece

parts.note: buster is American slang for a man, like dude

indicators.note: tail asks for the last letter of the bird's name

parts.note: Y is one of the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: A stormy petrel, a seabird linked with bad weather, is caught by some stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stormy petrel' reads as one bird; split, 'Stormy' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: weather with strong gusting winds is stormy.
